sermon.title: Lifting Hands
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer shows that believers are to proclaim God’s praises and lift their hands as Solomon and the Psalms did, showing allegiance to Jesus. Psalm 141:2 likens prayer to incense and lifted hands to the evening sacrifice, which Jesus fulfilled in his death and burial. At evening Ezra’s people wept in repentance, fire fell for Elijah, Gabriel came to Daniel, and the risen Jesus met and sent his disciples.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Points to check: Psalm 63:4 spoken as “63 verse 3”; Exodus 29:39 spoken as “29-30 9”; the Emmaus pair called “two apostles”; Jewish hour segments explanation; “Muslims show their allegiance to Muhammad” when bowing. Sensitive content kept as spoken: “secular scientific idiots” on an eclipse; Mormons and Jehovah’s Witnesses as false religions; men called hard-headed and macho; dependence on megachurch and TV ministers.

faqs.question: Is proclaiming God’s praises optional?
faqs.answer: He says if you’re not, you’re disobeying.

faqs.question: Why lift hands in worship?
faqs.answer: Because God said to, showing allegiance to Jesus.

faqs.question: Who gets credit when worship is good?
Is lifting hands a Pentecostal practice?
faqs.answer: No, it’s scriptural in both testaments.

faqs.question: What is lifting hands compared to?
Was the darkness at the cross an eclipse?
faqs.answer: He says no eclipse lasts three hours.

faqs.question: When was Jesus buried?
faqs.answer: At evening, the time of the evening sacrifice.

faqs.question: Can we meet God apart from Sunday?
Who receives the Holy Ghost?
faqs.answer: All believers, not just Pentecostals and charismatics.
